_: ENGLISH KEY TEXT. First pass, authored 2026-09-10 against robin (dreame.vacuum.r2469a, L10s Ultra Gen 2, pad - wash+empty - tanks=yes). That emission covers 424 of 700 models, the largest regime in the catalogue, and it is the only one with a machine-in-hand record (a hand walk of the machine on 2026-09-09, kept outside the repository).
_dust_bin_and_filter: The one panel whose heading names two objects, so these steps carry nouns. Chris folded them together at hand walk 03:58 - the filter body is attached to the bin.
_lexicon: WHERE DREAME'S PRINTED ENGLISH NAMES THE PART, USE THEIR WORD. It is neutral by construction, it matches what is moulded or printed on the machine, and it matches the panel heading the card renders above the step. That is why this file says Acoustic Foam, Caster Wheel and descaler rather than my own coinages. en is the card's BUNDLED UNIVERSAL FALLBACK (guide-loader.js), so a Dutch or Korean user sees it on a miss - but it is NOT the translation source, so a regionalism never propagates into the other 17.
_main_brush: Anchor names the guard but not how it opens. The compartment wipe is Chris's addition, 2026-09-10 - the manuals only ever describe the part, never the cavity.
_mop_cloth: cloth + SimuMop, 132 models. ORDERING NOTE, settled 2026-09-11: the D9 manual carries a warning we deliberately DO NOT write - [D9 manual, mop-cleaning warning: take the pad off the module before cleaning, and keep dirty water away from the water outlet] The tank is CLEAN water; the dirty water is what comes off the PAD while you rinse. So it is a warning about DOING THE STEPS IN THE WRONG ORDER, and our sequence already prevents it - the pad comes off before anything is rinsed. Chris: pouring first or taking the pad off first "either works" - and that is the point, the note is unnecessary under ANY ordering where the pad is off before the rinse. A note that restates what the sequence already enforces is what made the old guides 1,597 lines. THE INVISIBLE JOB IS THAT THE MODULE HOLDS WATER - pull it off over a carpet and you find out the hard way. The air-hole line is a DIAGNOSTIC, not a step: source F10 manual, [F10 manual, water-tank section: it treats a blocked air hole in the tank cover as the cause of slow or uneven water flow] SimuMop folds in here - the S10 Polish text and the E20 English text are the same three beats.
_mop_pad: Chris's own sequence, which beats the manual: the L40s document prints the pad and the holder as two disconnected entries and never says they come apart as one job. Four items because a pad machine carries two of each - this is the only place mop_count reaches a step.
_mop_pad_holders: The Matrix10 Multi-Mop Switching Dock, 15 models. The dock parks three mop assemblies in Slot A / Slot B / Slot C and swaps them by room type, so the robot drops off and collects and THE USER NEVER TOUCHES THE ROBOT'S MOPS - the whole task is dock-side. Source: the Matrix10 Multi-Mop Switching Dock manual (EN+), maintenance section - it has the user remove and clean the mop pad holders, reinstall each into its own slot on the base station door, and fit each new pad to the holder of the matching colour.
_mop_roller: 94 models. THE INVISIBLE JOB IS THE FILTER AT THE BACK OF THE COMPARTMENT - you would never know it was there. Source S70 Roller: [S70 Roller manual, mop-assembly removal: release button, lift the assembly out, then wipe the compartment AND the filter behind it with a soft dry cloth]
_mop_track: 15 models. THE INVISIBLE JOB IS THAT HAIR TANGLES IN THE BRACKET, NOT THE MOP - clean the mop, refit it, and the tangle is still there. The reassurance is the manual's: the slot turning by itself during installation is normal. Source: the Aqua10 Ultra Track manual; its step 1 is a press-and-slide-the-clip-at-the-illustrated-angle instruction - the exact shape this project does NOT write, because it leans on an illustration the reader does not have.
_omnidirectional_wheel: The wheel comes OUT OF THE MACHINE - Chris did that on the hand walk. What he did NOT do is separate the axle from the tire, which is the manual's screwdriver note and exactly the disassembly level we cut. Hand walk 03:19: 'There was hair on mine and I could pluck it off easily. A small pair of tweezers if your hands are too big.'
_robot_used_water_box: roller + track, 56 models. These mops are washed ON THE ROBOT as it runs, so the robot has to store the dirty water - pads and cloth don't recycle it and have no such box. Source Z50 Ultra / Aqua20: [Z50 Ultra / Aqua20 manual, used-water-box section: release buttons, pour out, rinse with clean water, dry, reinstall]
_robot_water_tank: 149 models - every machine with no dock tanks carries its own water. EMPTY IS THE CORRECT RESTING STATE and refilling is the exception; this is the manual's own advice turned positive. Source E20: [E20 manual, storage advice: remove the 2-in-1 tank when charging or idle and pour out any remaining water, against mildew and odour]
_rules: TASK ALTITUDE. 'Access the dust bin and filter', never 'press the clip at the illustrated angle'.
NEVER STATE ACCESS TYPE. Screw or clip, one brush or two - the user is holding it.
THE CARD PRINTS THE COMPONENT NAME AS THE PANEL HEADING, so steps need not name it.
A SHARED KEY CARRIES NO PRONOUN AND NO NOUN - gender agreement breaks in 10 of 18 languages.
A COMPONENT-SPECIFIC KEY MAY USE A PRONOUN, because its referent never changes.
NO REASSEMBLY STEPS - parts are geometry-keyed. return_to_service absorbs the refit.
A NEGATIVE ONLY EARNS ITS PLACE WHERE THE USER HAS A REASON TO DO THE WRONG THING.
_sensors: Chris, hand walk 04:53: 'I will say clean dry soft cloth for sensors.' The note survives because people reach for a damp cloth on a stubborn mark - that is a real reason to do the wrong thing.
_shared: These six appear in more than one component and MUST stay object-free.
_side_brush: The manuals say only 'remove and clean the side brush'. Nothing was invented beyond that.
_washboard: The tray the mops are scrubbed against. Generic for now - roller docks add acoustic foam and track docks replace this with a washboard filter plus a heating module descale. Chris has not ruled on those.
_water_tanks: Chris's sequence, 2026-09-10. Dirty first, because that is the one that smells. 'Room-temperature' is Dreame's own phrase, borrowed from their plumbing section; the standalone 'do not add hot water' warning (723 occurrences) is dropped because nobody fills a vacuum from a kettle.
access.brush_guard: Release the brush guard and lift the brush out.
access.dust_bin: Open the robot cover and take out the dust bin.
access.station_door: Open the door on the front of the base station.
contacts.dock_side_too: Do the same for the charging contacts and the signal area on the dock.
dry.fully_before_refit: Allow to dry fully before putting it back.
filter.remove_and_tap: Lift the filter out and tap it gently to shake the dust loose.
mop.cloth_module_off: Release the mopping module and lift it off the robot.
mop.cloth_pad_off_module: Pull the mop pad off the module and clean both.
mop.cloth_pour_out_water: Pour out any water left in the module before you go any further.
mop.compartment_and_filter: Wipe out the mop compartment and the filter at the back of it, so nothing blocks the airflow.
mop.holders_remove: Lift the mop pad holders out of their slots.
mop.holders_to_corresponding_slots: Put each holder back in the slot it came out of. The dock picks a mop by its slot, so a holder in the wrong slot sends the wrong pad to the wrong room and nothing will tell you.
mop.pad_carriages_off: Lift the mop carriages off the robot.
mop.pad_clean_all_four: Clean all four parts - both pads and both carriages.
mop.pad_off_carriage: Peel each mop pad off its carriage.
mop.pads_off_holders_and_clean: Peel the pads off the holders and clean both. The colours are matched - each pad belongs on the holder of the same colour.
mop.roller_release_and_lift: Take the mop assembly out of its compartment.
mop.track_detach_from_bracket: Lift the mop off its bracket.
mop.track_hair_in_bracket: Clear any hair wound around the bracket itself, not just the mop.
mop.track_release_assembly: Release the mop assembly and take it out of the robot.
note.filter_no_brush_finger_sharp: Never clean the filter with a brush, a fingertip or anything sharp - it tears the mesh and the filter stops sealing.
note.see_user_manual: For detailed instructions and warnings, refer to your User Manual.
note.side_brush_do_not_yank: If the hair is wound on tight, work it loose or cut it free rather than pulling hard - the bristles bend and don't recover.
note.wet_cloth_damages_sensors: Keep the cloth dry. Moisture gets behind the sensor windows and they don't come back.
rinse.bin_and_filter_clean_water: Rinse the dust bin and the filter with clean water only.
service.return_to_dock: Put the robot back on its dock.
side.rinse_if_soiled: If it has picked up something wet or sticky, rinse it with clean water and let it dry fully before putting it back.
tool.remove_tangled_hair: Remove any tangled hair, using a suitable tool if it doesn't come loose by hand.
washboard.allow_cooling_before_service: If you have a heated washboard tray, allow ample time to fully cool before performing maintenance.
washboard.filter_if_fitted: If your base station has a washboard filter, rinse that too and put it back.
washboard.remove: Lift the washboard out of the base station.
washboard.wipe_base: Wipe out the tray underneath it.
wheel.omnidirectional_remove: Pull the wheel out of its socket.
wheel.wipe_other_wheels: Wipe the main wheels and any other wheels underneath with a dry cloth.
wipe.compartment_soft_dry_cloth: Wipe out the empty compartment with a soft, dry cloth.
wipe.soft_dry_cloth: Wipe clean with a soft, dry cloth.
